attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, after quoting Katja Grace. The sentence itself is his.

semantics.note: 'Aren't going to be able' is firm future language with no deadline, so it counts as an open-ended forecast. It reads largely as a remark about humility, but the wording is not hedged.

contract.note: The plain reading (justified accuracy, not just formatting) is fair and ordinary. Since no deadline was given, the forecast can only be supported by an impossibility result, which is a demanding but logically required test.

evidence.note: FRI study finding that near-term accuracy does not pick out credible long-term risk forecasters. It shows current limits but contains no impossibility result and no validated method.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. The packet shows no validated three-decimal method (which would contradict it) and no decisive impossibility result (which would support it). Without a conclusive event, it cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own observation in his own post.

semantics.note: Shortening 'a really large fraction' to 'a large fraction' is acceptable, and the scope (the AI and AI-adjacent community, doom and catastrophe risk) is kept.

contract.note: Reading the phrase as a substantial share, with no majority threshold, is fair and ordinary. Requiring a measure that separates unwillingness to discuss risk from skepticism about it matches his wording.

evidence.note: The 2022 AI Impacts survey predates the target period and measures risk beliefs, not willingness to discuss. A 17% response rate cannot be read as refusal.
Bengio's August 2023 account of disagreement among researchers. It is one person's testimony and does not measure how common unwillingness is.

reviews.rationale: No representative measure from August 2023 of willingness to discuss AI doom or catastrophe risk is in the packet. The items are context only, and the evidence neither supports nor contradicts the share Marcus asserted.

attribution.note: Marcus's own judgment of LeCun's post, in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the hedge that the conclusion 'might be true' and the core charge of no real argument. It is in substance an evaluative judgment of argument quality.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds that 'real argument' has no determinate standard: either an inference exists or it is adequately justified. The result would depend on a choice Marcus did not make.

evidence.note: LeCun's full post: it offers evolutionary and staff analogies, then simply asserts the design outcome. It is a personal post, not a company disclosure. Whether this counts as a real argument depends on the standard used.

reviews.rationale: The 'might be true' part is hedged and not scored. 'Hasn't given a real argument' is an evaluative judgment with no determinate test. LeCun's post contains premises, but whether they amount to a real or circular argument is a matter of interpretation.

attribution.note: Marcus's own footnote, judging Yudkowsky's position in his own words.

semantics.note: An observation about the evidential status of the claim that superintelligence will dominate by default. 'Seems' softens the tone but makes no probability claim. The core assertion is firm.

contract.note: The plain readings of 'default' and 'proven' (substantiated, not mathematically certain) are fair and ordinary. The support and contradiction conditions are balanced.

evidence.note: Yudkowsky's TIME essay states the argument as an expectation and assumes an opposed superintelligence. It is a primary statement, not a demonstration.
AGI Ruin presents 'no pivotal weak acts' as a premise he asserts, not one he establishes. This is a primary text, though the packet labels it a secondary summary.
Turner et al. (January 2023) say their results do not prove superintelligent agents will seek power. This leaves a key step unestablished.
The follow-up paper extends the power-seeking results but frames them as a possible risk, not default extinction. It supports plausibility without contradicting the claim.

reviews.rationale: As of August 2023, the main formal work said outright that it did not prove superintelligent agents would seek power. Yudkowsky's own texts present expectations and asserted premises. The record shows a plausible risk that had not been demonstrated as the default, as Marcus said.
